reasons.reason: A CLI command runs in a terminal against a project's files; no page renders it and no browser loads it.
These commands change catalogs, generated files and imports; they never reach the compiler, which is the only place a URL policy is read.
XLIFF export and import read and write catalog files at build time; no page, browser or URL policy is involved.
The toolkit runs at build time in Node and is kept out of every browser graph; the focused consumer proves that absence.
An application runs one URL policy, so each policy row is exercised in its own column.

The request handler answers requests on the server: a build has no request for it to answer and fails on a declaration made while prerendering (spec 07 section 5), a client navigation sends it no document request, and no browser runs it.
Server rendering configuration is read only by the server bundle; the browser bundle never imports it.
The server seat renders one response and reads it; nothing boots on a client after it.
Testing helpers run in a test runner; a build's prerender never loads them.

Equator produces the sitemap files as data, and the deployment writes or serves them to crawlers as they are (spec 07 section 11); no render of the application produces them and no page boots from them.
A caching declaration becomes a response header the server writes; no browser runs it, and a client navigation or hydration makes no document request.

A prerendered page has no response to carry a caching header; what the class does to a build is refuse a per-visitor or not-stored route and write no page for it (spec 07 section 9), which verify:consumer requires of the lazy route.

A renderer states what it decided with no page rendered at all (spec 07 section 5), so its answer is never a server-rendered page; verify:consumer claims both from the server's answers for the withdrawn and the unreachable dossier.

It describes the response a declaration produces. A build writes no page for a declared outcome (spec 07 section 5, checked by verify:consumer for the topic page), and a client navigation or a hydrated page has no response, which a release must not synthesize, so no build and no browser has a response for it to describe.

A page that declares its outcome while prerendering has no request to answer, so its render fails and no page is written (spec 07 section 5); verify:consumer lists the topic page for prerender with a value for each outcome and requires the refusal.
An alias is a second prefix a path-prefix policy accepts; the neutral and host policies have no prefix to alias.
Node 22 has no Intl.DurationFormat, so no duration can be formatted there; the exercise sheet holds Equator to the typed result spec 08 section 3 requires instead.
